title: Group Chat and Semester
premise: Marguerite Ashgrove, a debate champion whose home life is a losing argument she can't win, discovers her late grandmother's recipe box holds coded instructions for a secret society of students who trade favors and secrets to survive their elite semester. Pulled into the group chat that runs it all, Marguerite must decide whether power is worth the price of becoming what she's fighting. When the society demands she destroy her best friend's audition chances to secure her own survival, she chooses truth over leverage — exposing the system, losing the friendship, and finally winning the argument at home by refusing to play at all.
about_author: Yara Reyes is a former high school debater from San Antonio who writes about ambitious girls and the systems they're told to be grateful for. She collects recipe boxes and believes every family keeps at least one secret in a kitchen drawer.

chapters.title: The Losing Argument
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. At the state debate final, Marguerite wins flawlessly; at dinner that night, she can't get a single sentence past her exhausted mother and bitter father. Emotional beat: the gap between public brilliance and private powerlessness, establishing what 'fine' costs her.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Sorting grandma's recipe box after the funeral, she finds cards with no food — measurements that map the school, ingredients that are names. A card labeled 'Semester Stew' lists five students including her. Beat: grief sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: You've Been Added
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. A group chat called 'Kitchen' adds her overnight; messages arrive like recipes: 'one favor, folded gently.' Her best friend Priya is already a member and goes pale when Marguerite mentions it. Beat: the thrill of being chosen curdling into unease.

chapters.title: First Course
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The society grants her first wish — a teacher's grade quietly corrected — and asks nothing yet. Priya warns her debts here compound like interest. Beat: intoxication of effortless power versus instinct that nothing is free.

chapters.title: The Ledger Nobody Writes Down
chapters.summary: POV Theo, a senior member. Through his eyes we see how the Kitchen runs on unrecorded favors and quiet threats, and how he once tried to leave. Beat: sympathy for a complicit insider; the machine shown from inside its gears.

chapters.title: Audition Season
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Conservatory final auditions loom; Priya's piano audition is her whole future. The Kitchen offers Marguerite a guaranteed slot — if she delivers something on Priya. Beat: the first demand that costs someone she loves.

chapters.title: What Grandma Actually Cooked
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Digging through her grandmother's letters, she learns the old woman founded the Kitchen to protect scholarship kids — and was destroyed by it. Beat: inheritance reframed; the recipe box becomes a warning, not an invitation.

chapters.title: Small Debts, Loud Interest
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Her corrected grade surfaces as leverage; a member implies her mother's job could use a friend. Marguerite realizes she's collateral now. Beat: fear replacing flattery; the trap closing softly.

chapters.title: Priya's Hands
chapters.summary: POV Priya. We see Priya practicing until her wrists ache, hiding family money trouble, and noticing Marguerite lying badly. Beat: dramatic irony deepens — the friendship strained by secrets neither names.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The Kitchen votes on 'pruning' Priya's audition — sabotaging her slot to free one up. Marguerite argues against it and loses, learning the group's rules reward loyalty, not logic. Beat: her greatest skill fails her where it matters most.

chapters.title: Folded Gently
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Ordered to execute the sabotage, Theo hesitates and quietly gives Marguerite the proof of how slots are really allocated. Beat: a crack in the machine; complicity meets conscience.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine (Obviously)
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Performing normalcy at a family dinner while carrying the sabotage plan, she finally snaps and tells her parents a partial truth — and is shocked when her mother believes her. Beat: first honest conversation at home; the theme of truth begins paying dividends.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The Kitchen, sensing her wavering, sweetens the deal: betray Priya and they'll fix her family's finances permanently. Marguerite stalls, buying time with a lie she hates herself for. Beat: temptation at its most personal; corruption offered as rescue.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Room Confessions
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya confronts Marguerite with what she's overheard; Marguerite confesses everything except her own complicity. Priya walks out. Beat: the friendship breaks not over betrayal but over the lie protecting it.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Decoding grandma's final card, she finds instructions for dissolving the Kitchen — a mechanism requiring a member to publicly surrender every favor they've received. Beat: hope with a price tag; the climax's mechanism revealed.

chapters.title: Sweeping the Floor
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo chooses his side, copying the Kitchen's real ledger before they can purge it. Beat: redemption arc pivots; the insider risks everything for the outsider's plan.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. On audition day, the sabotage activates — Priya's slot vanishes mid-performance. Instead of retreating, Marguerite interrupts the panel and tells the whole room the truth about the Kitchen, invoking the dissolution clause aloud. Beat: climax; truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Interest Due
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The clause works: every favor unravels, including hers — grades, opportunities, reputation. Administrators circle, members scatter, and Marguerite stands stripped of everything the Kitchen gave her. Beat: the price of survival paid in full; devastation with dignity.

chapters.title: What You Can't Unsay
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya learns Marguerite refused the deal twice before the audition and burned her own future to save Priya's slot. She doesn't forgive yet — but she shows up. Beat: grief and gratitude coexisting; repair begun, not completed.

chapters.title: Home Economics
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. With no leverage left, Marguerite has only honesty — and for the first time, the argument at home ends in listening instead of winning. Her mother shares her own history with the Kitchen's predecessor. Beat: identity rebuilt without power; family arc resolved.

chapters.title: Empty Box
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The school investigates; Theo testifies; the Kitchen dissolves into ordinary student government. Marguerite returns grandma's recipe cards to the archive, keeping only the blank ones. Beat: aftermath; legacy reclaimed as choice rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: Second Semester
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Priya re-auditions and earns her place fairly; the two friends begin again, awkwardly, honestly. Marguerite joins the debate team not to win arguments but to start them. Beat: resolution — power renounced, identity chosen, survival redefined as truth-telling.
